prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create one new water-only lake miniature for caspian sea. Reference 1 is the actual geographic silhouette: preserve its north-up outline, proportions, islands, holes, bays and separate water bodies VERY faithfully, smoothing only the map's tiny angular sampling edges. Reference 2 is approved Loch Ness and supplies ONLY blue resin/water material, upper-left light, texture and subtle depth, NOT shape. The result is a translucent blue resin casting of the lake's WATER VOLUME only, mounted slightly off a vertical museum display wall. The entire map face is parallel to the screen and seen nearly head-on with no foreshortening. A very thin band of depth is visible along TOP-facing edges because the camera is just slightly above; never a thick extruded bottom fascia. Rich deep blue water, turquoise edge highlights, fine natural ripples and reflected silvery glints; retain sufficient blue opacity to read clearly against purple #392885. Natural map contour, not an arbitrary blob. Subject centred and occupies 90-94% of square canvas longest side with safe transparent margins. TRUE transparent background, remove white map-reference background. NO terrain, land rim, surrounding water, map markings, labels, pedestal, shelf, cast shadow or caustics outside the subject; those will be separate. No perspective rotation.
